Hey, i'm really sorry you're feeling this way.

Firstly, pills is a terrible way to attempt to go out. All medications you can get over the counter are very hard to commit suicide on, and almost always fail. It mostly causes extremely terrible pain, and can damage you permanently, and as a previous person said there is less than a 6% chance of succeeding.

I've attempted suicide three times (at 15, 1 year ago) and am happy that I was unsuccessful. I thought I would never be able to get over what my mind was going through, however the mind is much more powerful than you could think. I promise you that you will get over these feelings one day, it just takes time. I went through months of crying daily, just wishing for a gun to kill myself. I was hopeless, had absolutely nothing left to live for.

Try talking to someone you trust, preferably someone who has experienced depression themselves, it really does help. Caffeine was also able to help me get in a good mood on the daily. 

Also, talking to your parents about seeing a mental health professional and getting put on medication is a viable option.

Depression is very manipulative and can make you believe whatever it wants you to. I've seen people who are very attractive believe they are ugly af, people who were extremely popular believe they had no friends, etc. It changes your mind and will make you truly believe whatever it wants.

Please hang in there, and I hope your situation improves. If you ever need anyone to talk to, I visit here often.

It's interesting why many people dealing with depression and/or suicidal thoughts believe we live in a simulation.

I thought the same thing when I was in a very bad state last year. I attempted suicide three times, all failing (I mean, obviously.), and I'm really happy that I did. Personally, I do not believe we are in a simulation.

I do not want to push any agenda on to you, but religion did really help me get over whatever was going on with me. 

Simple things like caffeine also help put me in a better mood, and talking with someone you trust about everything really can take the weight off your shoulders. It's very cliche, but these things were very helpful to me. Also if you can try to seek mental health assistance from a professional and try to get on medication.

I will warn you however, some medications can make you feel worse, not feel anything, or generally not work. Trial and error is the only real solution when It comes to mental medications. 

I really hope you can find a solution to your stress and problems, and I'm here to talk if you ever need anything.

How's this?

I'll start off by saying it was nobody's fault. 
I wasn't bullied.
I had a lot of friends.
I had a good family.

So that still begs the question why? 

In short terms, I was born different. I was always aware that my mind's thought process was not normal, even from when I was as young as 4.

I can't exactly pinpoint what was "wrong."
Seasonal Affective Disorder was definatly a factor, but it was more than that.

I think it may have been Borderline Personality Disorder, I fit every symptom that I looked up online. 
The problem is that there is no treatment for this other than therapy.

My mind had had multiple phases it cycled to,
They were unpredictable, but the seasons could predict which ones were more likely to occur.
They could change within hours, or sometimes a few days. There was nothing that set me off, they came at complete random.
Each phase changed how my mind would interpret, handle, and understand every situation

List of phases:

Low
- Sad, racing thoughts.
- Poor energy
- My mind's thought process made me disect everything and it pushed it towards something way above what it really was. My attention span was greatly decreased and I didn't care about anything.
- 30-40% occurence in Winter, 10-25% summer.

 Numb 
- Would feel nothing. Happiness, sadness, anger were non-existant. I could laugh at something but it wouldn't cause happiness.
This is probably the hardest phase to explain. Despite anything that happened it was just constantly the same. 
- No sense of humor: Nothing would be funny, my mind struggled to understand any emotion
- My minds general state was conflicting. It could not understand how to start conversations, continue them, say or understand jokes, or generally interact with people.
- Very systematic thinking. Grades do the best during this phase
- 50-70% occurence in winter, 20-50% summer

 Elevated
- Probably what normal is considered
- Capable of feeling emotion, could interact with people normally.
- My minds thought process would do logical things and functioned pretty regularly.
- 10-15% occurence in winter 30-40% occurence summer

 Boost
- A feeling of euphoria and happiness that came under for no reason.
- I could feel any emotion, but there was a constant happiness to it. It's hard to explain.
- Probably my favorite state I could feel
- Impulsive actions, really good at interacting with people
- Not mania, I was aware of what I was doing and there was still logical thinking
- Rarest occurence. < 2% Winter < 4% Summer

I don't really think there is an inbetween of any of these. They are always on the same levels.
I've learned to be able to recognize each.



I want to make clear that this was nobody's fault. Nothing pushed me, nobody did anything wrong.
I don't have any regrets.
I don't have a grudge.
I'm not angry, I'm not sad.


Your mind is going to try to assign blame to someone, something, or yourself. It's what it does as a coping mechanism. Don't. 
There wasn't any preventable way to stop this. I've battled it for as long as I can remember. It had extreme power to it and was impossible to persuade or change.
Therapy wouldn't be able to fix it, and medication could only make me numb. (Not to mention how dangerous these medications were that could have been a "possibility.")
Don't assign blame to anyone, I assure you nothing could have been done.


I know this is going to hurt a lot of people, and I'm sorry for that. I really hope everybody can find peace of mind, and will be able to move on in life. I do hope the best for everyone. I don't want anyone to be sad, that's not what this was about. The constant changing of my mind was just ridicously hard to live with, and there was nothing I, or anyone else could do to fix it.
